note: Next-generation GAA enzymes after alglucosidase: cipaglucosidase alfa (with miglustat) approved 2023 on one trial plus Gaa KO mouse confirmatory evidence; reveglucosidase alfa dropped after phase 3 start; clervonafusp alfa (VAL-1221) terminated for funding without results.
label: Pompe disease (next-gen GAA)

engagement.judgement: Opening entry at the first published member-drug use of the Gaa KO mouse (the strain itself dates from 1998).
engagement.note: Reveglucosidase alfa (GILT-tagged GAA) cleared skeletal-muscle glycogen better than rhGAA in Gaa KO mice; no patient glycogen readout yet.
engagement.short: KO mice: better muscle glycogen clearance
engagement.quote: GILT-tagged GAA was significantly more effective than rhGAA in clearing glycogen from numerous skeletal muscle tissues in the Pompe mouse model.

engagement.magnitude_basis: urinary Hex4 change vs alglucosidase against mouse tissue glycogen clearance vs alglucosidase
engagement.confidence_note: FDA integrated review read (section 6.1.4); model side Xu 2019 abstract. PROPEL paper (Schoser 2021) may have reported Hex4 earlier; full text not read, so dated to the review/registry posting.
engagement.judgement: Paired by me: mouse tissue glycogen (Xu 2019) against urinary Hex4, a downstream glycogen biomarker, in PROPEL. Reveglucosidase alfa has no comparable patient glycogen readout found.
engagement.note: Mice showed cipaglucosidase+miglustat clearing more glycogen than alglucosidase; in PROPEL urinary Hex4 fell 1.88 vs rose 1.22 mmol/mol on alglucosidase.
engagement.short: Hex4 fell more than on alglucosidase
engagement.quote: Reductions in CK and Hex4 were significantly greater with cipa-mig than with the comparator.
engagement.reason: Glycogen biomarker fell as mice predicted

engagement.model: Human whole-blood / neutral-pH enzyme stability assay (cipaglucosidase alfa with miglustat)
engagement.note: Ex vivo, cipaglucosidase alfa lost 70% activity in human blood over 4 h; miglustat prevented the loss, predicting higher active-enzyme exposure in patients.
engagement.short: Miglustat keeps enzyme active in blood
engagement.quote: In contrast, when cipaglucosidase alfa alone was incubated with whole human blood for 4 h, it lost 70% of its enzymatic activity.
engagement.confidence_note: Year is a proxy: first-in-human ATB200-02 (NCT02675465), which tested miglustat co-dosing, started 2016; study RRB200-040 itself is undated in the review.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry at the first clinical use of the stabilisation rationale.

engagement.model: Human whole-blood / neutral-pH enzyme stability assay (cipaglucosidase alfa with miglustat)
engagement.magnitude_basis: ex vivo: 70% activity loss without vs very little with miglustat over 4 h; patients: plasma GAA activity AUC0-t +7.1%/+3.7%, AUCtmax-24h +24%/+21.3% with 130/260 mg miglustat
engagement.note: In ATB200-02, miglustat raised plasma GAA activity and protein exposure versus cipaglucosidase alone, but by under 50%, far less than the ex vivo stabilisation implied.
engagement.quote: Overall, the PK results showed that coadministration of cipaglucosidase alfa with miglustat resulted in increases in plasma levels of total GAA protein and GAA activity compared to cipaglucosidase alfa administered alone, which supported that miglustat stabilized cipaglucosidase alfa
engagement.confidence_note: FDA integrated review read (section on contribution of miglustat, Table 30, in vitro evidence). Quote ends mid-sentence. No earlier tier 1 publication of the ATB200-02 with/without-miglustat PK found; dated to the 2023 review.
engagement.reason: Exposure rose, smaller than ex vivo
engagement.judgement: Comparison stated: the FDA review sets the clinical PK beside the in vitro stabilisation data in one assessment. Scored same with partial: direction held, but the review calls the enhancement relatively small (<50%), with no exposure-response link to efficacy.

dose.confidence_note: Year is a proxy: first-in-human ATB200-02 (NCT02675465) started April 2016; the margin is documented in the 2023 FDA review.
dose.model: Rat and cynomolgus monkey repeat-dose toxicology (exposure margin)
dose.note: NHP toxicology gave a 31-55-fold AUC margin for the 5 mg/kg starting dose of cipaglucosidase alfa with miglustat.
dose.short: NHP tox margin set starting dose
dose.quote: The predicted safety margin for 5 mg/kg cipaglucosidase alfa starting dose was 31- to 55-fold in area under the concentration-time curve (AUC) and 23- to 55-fold in maximum concentration (Cmax).

dose.magnitude_basis: dose reached (20 mg/kg) vs model-stated tolerated exposure
dose.confidence_note: FDA integrated review read. Clinical side: the same review concludes cipa-mig 'is safe for its intended use'; only hypersensitivity (a class effect) led to discontinuations.
dose.judgement: The model stated a tolerated margin, not an efficacious exposure; 20 mg/kg was chosen to match alglucosidase. Scored only the toxic end (Decision 16). The quote begins mid-sentence in the review.
dose.model: Rat and cynomolgus monkey repeat-dose toxicology (exposure margin)
dose.note: 26-week monkey study clean at 18.1x the 20 mg/kg exposure; patients were dosed to 20 mg/kg with miglustat without dose-limiting organ toxicity.
dose.quote: gross necropsy observations, organ weights or histopathology were observed at doses up to 200 mg/kg/day (about 18.1 times the exposure at the MRHD of 20 mg/kg ABT200, via AUC).

efficacy.note: Gaa KO mice predicted next-generation GAA would beat rhGAA; first member data (reveglucosidase alfa) published 2012.
efficacy.quote: GILT-tagged GAA was significantly more effective than rhGAA in clearing glycogen from numerous skeletal muscle tissues in the Pompe mouse model.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: mouse PIF/PEF vs patient MIP/MEP improvement, as the authors describe
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (JPET paywalled). Retrodiction status inferred: the paper cites the patient data (Byrne, in preparation) from a trial running since 2011; study dates not verified.
efficacy.judgement: Separate track (plethysmography is a different readout). The patient comparator (MIP/MEP) was exploratory in a safety-primary phase 1/2, and the INSPIRE MIP primary (+2.2% at week 24, single-arm, terminated) was never inferentially tested.
efficacy.note: Reveglucosidase alfa stabilised peak inspiratory/expiratory flow in Gaa KO mice, which the authors matched to MIP/MEP gains in phase 1/2 patients.
efficacy.quote: Improvement of murine PIF and PEF were similar in magnitude to increases in maximal inspiratory and expiratory pressure observed clinically in late onset Pompe patients treated with Reveglucosidase alfa

efficacy.magnitude_basis: 6MWD difference vs alglucosidase (13.6 m, 95% CI -2.8 to 29.9) against mouse superiority in glycogen and muscle function
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level for Schoser 2021 and Xu 2019; FDA review read (it cites the KO-mouse data as confirmatory evidence). Registry NCT03729362 results posted 2023-09-11.
efficacy.judgement: Judgement call: the mouse predicted superiority over alglucosidase; the primary endpoint moved in that direction (13.6 m LOCF; 5.3 m in the FDA MMRM) but missed significance. Scored same, partial, not contra, because direction agreed and FDA accepted the mouse data as confirmatory evidence. Reveglucosidase trials had safety primaries or were single-arm and terminated, so they change no status.
efficacy.note: Mice showed cipaglucosidase+miglustat superior to alglucosidase; PROPEL 6MWD favoured it by 13.6 m but missed statistical superiority.
efficacy.quote: Cipaglucosidase alfa plus miglustat did not achieve statistical superiority to alglucosidase alfa plus placebo for improving 6-min walk distance in our overall population of patients with late-onset Pompe disease.

patient_trials.quote: Percent Predicted Maximum Inspiratory Pressure (MIP): change from baseline to week 24 2.2 (SD 8.3) on reveglucosidase alfa; INSPIRE terminated by sponsor decision.

Subjects receiving 20 mg/kg of reveglucosidase alfa demonstrated increases in predicted maximum inspiratory pressure (13.9%), predicted maximum expiratory pressure (8.0%), forced vital capacity (-0.4%)

safety.confidence_note: Year is a proxy (ATB200-02 start April 2016).
safety.model: Rat and cynomolgus monkey repeat-dose toxicology
safety.note: 26-week rat and monkey studies of cipaglucosidase alfa, and 13-week monkey co-dosing with miglustat, found no target-organ toxicity.
safety.short: Tox clean in rats and monkeys
safety.quote: In a 26-week GLP study in monkeys (biweekly, IV, N=10), no clinical signs, effects on electrocardiography, effects on food consumption or body weights, ophthalmologic effects

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; Maga 2013 full text has no mention of glucose or insulin receptor. BioMarin's toxicology never published (no BLA filed).
safety.judgement: Hypoglycaemia is a harm animals could show (IGF2-tag binding to insulin/IGF receptors), but with the toxicology unpublished there is no model statement to score.
safety.note: Hypoglycaemia occurred in 63% of patients on IGF2-tagged reveglucosidase alfa; no published nonclinical study stated or excluded it.
safety.quote: The most common adverse events were hypoglycemia (63%), dizziness, fall, headache, and nausea (55% for each).

safety.magnitude_basis: absence of target-organ toxicity, animals vs patients
safety.confidence_note: FDA integrated review read. The rabbit embryo-fetal cardiovascular malformations (co-dosing, no NOAEL) have no patient comparison and are not scored.
safety.judgement: Judgement call: the anaphylaxis to a human protein is not scored as a miss, because animal immunogenicity to human biologics does not predict human hypersensitivity (the CRS rule).
safety.model: Rat and cynomolgus monkey repeat-dose toxicology
safety.note: No organ toxicity predicted and none seen in 151 LOPD patients; hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis, a class immunogenicity effect, was the main harm.
safety.quote: The available safety data show that cipaglucosidase alfa coadministered with miglustat is safe for its intended use.
